title: Dominic and the Horizon
premise: Rosalind Sterling has spent a decade running salvage digs across the world's margins, keeping her famous father's name off every contract and her heart in no port long enough to unpack. When her old rival Marcus Vane hires the crew for an expedition into the Karakoram to recover her father's lost final survey — the one job they swore off after the accident that killed her brother — she takes it only because refusing means someone worse will go. Trapped by monsoon floods with a leaking boat and a quiet stranger named Teodor who knows more about her family than he admits, Rosalind uncovers that her father's survey documents a stolen artifact and that Vane intends to bury the truth along with anyone who carries it. In the brief window when the glacier calving opens the high route, she must choose between the evidence that could restore her name and the lives of the crew, ultimately exposing Vane, reconciling with her dying father, and finding that belonging was never a place but the people who stayed.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who spent six seasons in the Himalayan foothills before trading rapids for manuscripts. Known for adventure fiction where landscapes are characters and survival is never the hardest part, Blackwood writes from a houseboat on an unnamed tributary.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She finishes a salvage dig in coastal Bangladesh, measuring her life in distances traveled, and refuses a call from her estranged father's nurse. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for freedom.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus Vane finds her at a dockside bar with a contract: lead a crew into the Karakoram for her father's lost final survey. She burns the contract; he leaves a copy anyway. Beat: old wounds reopened by ambition.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Rosalind assembles her usual misfits — engineer Priya, medic Okonkwo, teenage runner Dex — telling herself it's just another job. Beat: found-family warmth masking dread.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Route
chapters.summary: Her POV reviewing her brother Eli's old maps; the route passes the glacier where he died. Flashback to the accident ten years ago. Beat: grief surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: The crew travels river routes toward the mountains; first hints that Vane's funding comes from somewhere dirty. Priya notices sealed crates. Beat: unease beneath camaraderie.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Confluence
chapters.summary: They rescue Teodor, a quiet man stranded with a damaged boat who speaks fluent Karakoram dialects and knows her father's handwriting intimately. Beat: wary attraction and suspicion.

chapters.title: Monsoon Lock-In
chapters.summary: The rains close the passes early; the crew is trapped on a leaking boat in flooded gorges. Rosalind realizes Vane timed the trip deliberately. Beat: claustrophobia and dawning betrayal.

chapters.title: Bailing Water, Bailing Truth
chapters.summary: Teodor reveals he was her father's last assistant and that the survey documents a looted artifact Vane's backers want erased. Beat: trust tested by revelation.

chapters.title: Night on the Leaking Deck
chapters.summary: A storm nearly sinks them; Rosalind and Teodor keep the boat alive through the night, talking about Eli without naming him. Beat: intimacy forged in crisis.

chapters.title: What Vane Paid For
chapters.summary: They find Vane's advance team dead — silenced. Rosalind understands the expedition is a cleanup operation and she was hired as cover. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Dex's Discovery
chapters.summary: Teenage Dex finds a hidden cache with Eli's journal, proving the 'accident' involved the same artifact. Rosalind's POV shatters. Beat: rage and vertigo.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Rosalind decides not to run — for once, to stand. They radio no one and plan to reach the ice cave before Vane's remaining men. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Porters and Ghosts
chapters.summary: A village of porters shelters them; Rosalind learns her father sent money here for years, quietly making amends. Beat: complicated love for a flawed man.

chapters.title: The Glacier's Edge
chapters.summary: They trek to the calving glacier as monsoon ends; the route will open for days only. Vane's hunters close in behind. Beat: race against geology.

chapters.title: Ice Cave
chapters.summary: Inside the frozen cave they find the survey cache — and evidence Eli died protecting it. Rosalind reads his last pages aloud. Beat: catharsis and fury.

chapters.title: Vane Arrives
chapters.summary: Vane corners them at the cave mouth, offering Rosalind partnership and erasure of her past if she hands over the documents. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Climax: the glacier calves during the standoff; Rosalind uses the collapse to trap Vane's men, saves Vane himself against all instinct, and secures the evidence. Beat: justice chosen over vengeance.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Wounded, they carry everything down together; Vane, broken, confesses to authorities at the valley station. Beat: exhaustion and unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The Nurse's Number
chapters.summary: Rosalind finally calls her father. He is dying but lucid; their conversation is small, imperfect, real. Beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: The artifact is returned; the truth published under both Sterlings' names. Rosalind watches her father read his rehabilitation in a hospital bed. Beat: justice outside the law completed inside it.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Epilogue-ish: the crew debates the next contract; Rosalind unpacks her bag fully for the first time in ten years, in a town with people in it. Beat: belonging chosen.

chapters.title: Horizon, Not Escape
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Rosalind's POV: she and Teodor set out on a new survey — not fleeing, but going toward. The horizon reframed as invitation. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
